invariant: After Graphviz returns SVG, Java DotStringFactory.solve locates each cluster polygon, parses its serialized points, computes min/max from those decimal coordinates, and passes that reconstructed rectangle to Cluster.setPosition. Painted cluster geometry therefore uses the SVG polygon rectangle rather than Graphviz's higher-precision internal bounding box. A boundary such as 170.99 versus 171.00 is behaviorally significant for dimension-seeded symbols such as clouds.
causal_divergence: The Rust layout crate already returns both internal cluster_positions and cluster_serialized_sizes reconstructed from two-decimal polygon coordinates. Class rendering uses only the internal box. In the held-out linked empty-package matrix, the internal filled-cluster width is exactly 171 while Java's serialized rectangle is just below 171; cloud_frontier truncates the former to seed 171 and Java truncates the latter to seed 170, producing a wholly different path despite otherwise exact layout.
planned_change: Before class envelope normalization and paint, round each cluster origin to the SVG coordinate precision and replace its width/height with LayoutResult.cluster_serialized_sizes, matching DotStringFactory.solve. Preserve the internal graph extent for graph-level layout only. Exercise non-symbol and dimension-seeded symbol clusters around integer boundaries in both layout directions.
